statement: XLEN = 64. The integer registers and the supported user address space are 64 bits.
The *W instructions ignore the upper 32 bits of their inputs, produce a 32-bit signed result, and sign-extend it to 64 bits — bits XLEN-1 through 31 are equal. Overflow is ignored.
SLLI/SRLI/SRAI take a 6-bit shift amount from the I-immediate; SLL/SRL/SRA use only the low 6 bits of rs2. SLLIW/SRLIW/SRAIW take 5 bits, and SLLW/SRLW/SRAW use rs2[4:0].

SLLIW, SRLIW and SRAIW encodings with imm[5] != 0 are RESERVED. They were previously defined to raise an illegal-instruction exception; this revision marks them reserved instead, and calls the change backwards-compatible.

LUI places the 32-bit U-immediate in rd with the low 12 bits zeroed, sign-extended to 64 bits. AUIPC forms the same 32-bit offset, sign-extends it to 64 bits, and adds it to the address of the AUIPC instruction.
LW sign-extends its 32-bit result to 64 bits; LWU zero-extends it. LH/LB sign-extend and LHU/LBU zero-extend analogously. SD/SW/SH/SB store the low 64/32/16/8 bits of rs2.
A load with rd = x0 must still raise any exceptions and cause any other side effects, even though the loaded value is discarded.
JALR computes its target by adding the sign-extended 12-bit immediate to rs1 and then setting the least-significant bit of the result to zero.
Control transfers have no architecturally visible delay slots.

IALIGN = 32, because no 16-bit-length extension is included. An instruction-address-misaligned exception is therefore raised on a taken branch or unconditional jump whose target is not 4-byte aligned.
The instruction-address-misaligned exception is reported on the branch or jump, NOT on the target instruction. A branch that is not taken raises no such exception.
An instruction access-fault on the TARGET of a jump or taken branch is reported on the target instruction, not on the jump or branch — the opposite reporting point from misalignment.
Little-endian. The specification delegates this to the EEI; endianness in RISC-V is byte-address invariant.

Misaligned loads and stores are NOT handled invisibly. A misaligned access raises an address-misaligned exception, delivered as a CONTAINED trap reported to the harness. Access-fault is not substituted, because this profile declares no memory region with side effects.

Decoding a reserved instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception. The architecture declares this behaviour UNSPECIFIED and notes that platforms differ, so the model must record the outcome as a laboratory policy over an UNSPECIFIED case and must be able to report it as such.
Every code point in the RV64I HINT table executes as a no-op that writes nothing to x0's architectural value; a HINT must not trap. This profile implements no HINT behaviour beyond that.

FENCE is decoded and must not trap. With one hart, no external devices and an in-order model, it has no observable effect. FENCE.TSO (fm=1000, pred=RW, succ=RW) is accepted and treated as FENCE RW,RW, which the specification states is correct. Other fm values are reserved and fall under D-RESERVED-DECODE.

ECALL and EBREAK cause a precise REQUESTED trap to the execution environment. With no privileged modes in this profile there is no guest handler, so both are reported to the harness as a typed environment-trap outcome and execution stops unless the harness contract says otherwise.

At reset: pc = the declared entry address of the loaded image; x1..x31 = 0; x0 is architecturally 0 always. The base ISA does not define the initial contents of x1..x31 — the EEI does — so this is a harness declaration and guest programs may not assume any other environment provides it.

source_refs.locator: RISC-V Software Execution Environments and Harts

statement: A 64-bit byte-addressed space in which only the regions declared by the harness memory map are legal. An access outside a declared region raises an access-fault exception. The specification delegates which portions are legal to the execution environment.
The address space is CIRCULAR: the byte at address 2^XLEN-1 is adjacent to the byte at address 0, and address computations done by the hardware ignore overflow and wrap modulo 2^XLEN.
Every executed instruction entails an implicit memory read — the instruction fetch. Explicit reads and writes are made only by load and store instructions.

The set of locations implicitly readable for instruction fetch is the same as the set explicitly readable by loads in this laboratory. The specification allows the two sets to differ and delegates the choice to the execution environment; this profile declares them identical so that a fetch fault and a load fault at the same address are comparable.

The model re-reads memory for every instruction fetch, so a store that modifies a later-fetched instruction becomes visible immediately. This is a legal implementation choice but NOT an architectural guarantee: without the Zifencei extension (absent from this profile) the base ISA permits a hart to cache fetchable bytes and never re-read main memory, so a guest may not rely on this behaviour and a reference model that caches is not wrong.

Every region this profile declares is MAIN MEMORY: reads and writes have no visible side effects. The profile declares no I/O region, which is why D-MISALIGN-DATA can raise address-misaligned rather than substituting access-fault. A reference whose default platform supplies I/O regions must be configured to remove them before it is a matched profile — see D-PLATFORM.

The laboratory platform declares exactly one region — the MainMemory region of the harness memory map — and NO devices: no core-local interruptor, no interrupt generator, and no machine software, timer or external interrupt source. A reference model is not matched to this profile until its platform is configured to the same shape, not merely its instruction set.

source_refs.locator: RISC-V Software Execution Environments and Harts

statement: Memory is addressed in 8-bit bytes and every address is a 64-bit value interpreted modulo 2^64. The harness supplies and reports addresses in these units and no other.
The harness honours exactly the access widths this profile's loads and stores request — 8, 16, 32 and 64 bits — and rejects any other width as a contract violation rather than servicing it.

No time source is reachable by a guest. This profile excludes Zicntr, Zihpm and all CSRs, so no counter is architecturally readable — AND the laboratory platform declares no core-local interruptor, so no memory-mapped time register is readable either. ⛔ Both halves are required: excluding the CSR instructions alone does NOT exclude reading time, because a CLINT exposes mtime as ordinary MMIO that a plain load reaches. The harness's retired-instruction count is not target-visible and may not justify any guest-observable behaviour.

source_refs.locator: RISC-V Software Execution Environments and Harts

statement: The only events this profile delivers are synchronous exceptions and requested traps, raised at the instruction that caused them. No asynchronous interrupt is deliverable — because the laboratory platform declares no interrupt controller and no machine software, timer or external source, NOT because the instruction set lacks CSRs. A hart always runs in at least machine mode and its trap state exists whether or not Zicsr is present, so the absence must be a platform property to be real.

Execution is sequential and deterministic: one hart, in-order, each instruction's effects complete before the next instruction's begin. This profile makes NO memory-ordering claim — RVWMO is out of scope until MC-MULTICORE — and a guest may not rely on this harness's sequential behaviour as an architectural guarantee.

For every instruction fetch the harness supplies 32 bits from a declared executable region, or the specified failure. It performs no fetch that the model did not request, and no fetch has a side effect.

The harness establishes the declared entry state before the first fetch: pc at the loaded image's entry address, x1..x31 zeroed, memory outside the loaded image unwritten. Only a cold reset is modelled; there is no warm reset and no retained state to order.

source_refs.locator: RISC-V Software Execution Environments and Harts

statement: Every instruction in this profile's scope completes or faults as a unit: there is no multi-step or restartable suboperation in RV64I base, so no partially committed effect can be observed. A fault therefore leaves the architectural state exactly as it was before the faulting instruction, except for the fault report itself.
